original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,4,3), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every four points determine at least three distinct distances, equivalently a set with no squares.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 29: determine the asymptotic value of ϕ(n,4,3), immediately after the sentence identifying ϕ(n,4,3) as the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point set that does not span any squares. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the survey very closely: it names the correct parameter ϕ(n,4,3), asks for its asymptotic value, keeps the problem in the planar setting, states the local condition that every 4-point subset determines at least 3 distinct distances, and uses the paper’s own equivalent no-squares reformulation. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
missing_details: State the paper’s definition of ϕ(n,k,l) explicitly: it is a minimum over all n-point sets P⊂R^2 satisfying the stated local condition. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
Specify that the distances are Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of P. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Make the quantifier fully explicit as every 4-point subset of P, not just an informal every four points. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Make the asymptotic regime explicit as n→∞; the paper phrases the task as finding the asymptotic value of ϕ(n,4,3). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Spell out the forbidden-configuration wording precisely as no 4-point subset of P spans a square. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

If you want the question to reflect the nearby context as well as the bare problem statement, include the currently recorded bounds Ω(n/log n) ≤ ϕ(n,4,3) ≤ O(n/√log n). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

The subsection also states a convention that, here and in the following cases, degenerate polygons are considered when relevant; this does not materially change the square-free case, but it is part of the immediate context. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
refined_question: Let ϕ(n,k,l) denote the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P⊂R^2 such that every k-point subset of P determines at least l distinct distances. Determine, as n→∞, the asymptotic growth of ϕ(n,4,3). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P⊂R^2 such that no 4-point subset of P spans a square. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the survey because the local-properties section first defines ϕ(n,k,l), then in the k=4 case immediately specializes to ϕ(n,4,3), restates it in no-squares language, and poses exactly the open problem of finding its asymptotic value. The adjacent table gives the same parameter with bounds Ω(n/log n) and O(n/√log n), and the upper bound is tied to the triangular-lattice discussion in Section 2. In the June 2014 PDF draft mirrored on the author’s site, this same item appears as Section 6, Problem 28 on p. 12; in the current arXiv HTML version it is Section 7, Problem 29. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
